subject: Joint modelling - continuous and Time-to-Event model

messages.author: 7782d37d65009a99
messages.subject: Joint modelling - continuous and Time-to-Event model
parts:
Hi everyone, 

i am quite new to STAN and was wondering what the possibility is in STAN to estimate a joint model of continuous and Time-to-Event data. Is STAN a good and robust platform for this kind of analysis (what about convergence and fitting?)? As well, if there is any example code or past experience to share as a starting point, i would be very happy to take.
Thanks very much.

Best,
Camille

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Joint modelling - continuous and Time-to-Event model
parts:
Hi!

Stan is great for this kind of stuff. There is just the usual pill to swallow when you do Bayesian TTE that you need either a parametric baseline hazard or some non-parametric variant. In short: Partial likelihood is not enough.

Other than that I can tell from my own experience that you need to watch out for the parametrization. Standard TTE distributions parametrization are not always optimal for sampling; at least in my problems I came across. However, you are new, so you should get started and do those parametrization games in a second step (pairs plots, etc.).

Sebastian

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Joint modelling - continuous and Time-to-Event model
parts:
One thing that we've learned in different PKPD examples is that if a variable is measured with error, it makes sense to include that measurement error in the model (easy to do in Stan, not so easy with traditional non-Bayesian approaches).  More than once we've improved a model by taking some quantity that we've assumed was known, and replacing it with a measurement-error model.
A
